Set the modelling grid

Source: R/data-mt_data.R
mt_set_grid.Rd

The grid is the resolution on which models work. Every observed cell must be a union of grid cells, so the grid is at least as fine as the finest table. Without a grid set, the grid is the coarsest one on which every table is exact: the age groups of the data when all tables have the same groups, single years when one table (for example populations) has single years. Coarser grids are obtained with mt_regroup(), single years from grouped deaths with mt_ungroup().

Usage

mt_set_grid(data, age = NULL, period = NULL)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object.

age, period

mt_axis objects (NULL keeps the current axis).

Value

The updated mt_data object.

Examples

x <- mt_example()
x <- mt_set_grid(x, age = single_ages(30, 100))
mt_grid(x)$age
#> <mt_axis: age, 71 intervals> 30 31 32 33 ... 98 99 100+
